checks: Finiteness of the integer support gives q as the maximum affine fiber dimension and the top-dimensional fiber sum for intrinsic mass. Lower-dimensional fibers are null for that measure.

Vertical thickening leaves every sampled base unchanged. Applying the tube limit on each fiber and multiplying the lower ranks by ε^(q-r_z) gives the finite raw weak limit; its positive total gives normalized weak convergence.

Centers on the thickened traces have a compact subsequence limiting to an original mixed point. For any fixed containing closed halfspace, an outward relaxation eventually contains that same subsequence. Closed Portmanteau gives the lower bound, and decreasing the relaxation retains original boundary mass.

The limiting center is selected before the arbitrary halfspace, so no uniform convergence over halfspaces is needed. The full-volume premise is used only on the positive-volume thickenings. Source §3 matches and q=0 gives a counting measure over point fibers.

dependencies.hypotheses: Each old sampled fiber is a nonempty compact convex set in R^d of affine rank r_z; apply its exact orthogonal tube limit and use the common scaling ε^(-(d-q)).
dependencies.status: same-batch independent approval required before admission

overlap.comparison: Its parallel relaxation proves attainment at a fixed mixed measure. Here normalization and a changing weak limit transfer a universal constant to a different intrinsic measure.
It directly guarantees an intrinsic Helly bound depending on the affine rank and occupied parities. It does not transfer an arbitrary positive-volume constant unchanged.

readability: The closed enlarged cap is fixed before using Portmanteau, so positive mass on the original cap boundary is preserved.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The transfer from full-volume to intrinsic depth preserves the same constant and covers all closed boundaries, including q=0.
